correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening in São Francisco de Paula
correspondence.finding: The eastern opening occupies the small drainage network around the Cerrito/Capão do Cerrito–Mangueira de Pedras setting northeast of São Francisco de Paula's urban seat. The IBGE original shows these connected headward streams and the westward approach toward the Rio Santa Cruz reservoir corridor. The model's initial feeder is not asserted to be the report's cited Santa Cruz spring, nor is an adjacent arroio label imposed on it.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; exact initial feeder name unassigned

correspondence.component_scope: Blang, Salto and the separate Divisa/Paranhana connections
correspondence.finding: The westward upper route enters the branching Blang reservoir setting and proceeds toward the Salto impoundment at Eletra. The IBGE original independently shows the water-body outlines and continuing Santa Cruz corridor. SGB's original report map and its adapted single-line diagram distinguish the Divisa approach from the north, the Santa Cruz/Blang line, Salto and the separate transfer to UHE Bugres/Rio Paranhana across the drainage divide. The selected mainstem continues northwest/west downstream of Salto toward the Santa Cruz–Caí corridor; it does not follow the transfer tunnel or the Paranhana route.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; reservoir and artificial-transfer names remain context, not river aliases

correspondence.component_scope: Upper western bends and middle Caí
correspondence.finding: The route turns northwest around the Passo do Inferno/Cará sector, then west along the northern Canela–Gramado side and past the separate Caracol, Macaco and Piaí approaches. It follows the Caí north of Nova Petrópolis, bends southwest through the Vale Real/Feliz setting and south past Bom Princípio. The SEMA map's continuous line and repeated Caí labels, rather than basin membership alone, establish the corridor. SGB prose expressly distinguishes the upstream Santa Cruz name and its downstream transition in western São Francisco de Paula; no precise name-transition vertex is allocated.

correspondence.component_scope: São Sebastião do Caí, Montenegro and lower river
correspondence.finding: The selected river passes the separate Cadeia approach near São Sebastião do Caí, continues past Pareci Novo and the Maratá approach to Montenegro, makes the distinctive southeastward bend and continues south through the lower floodplain west of Nova Santa Rita. The separate Mineiro approach and the final eastward turn are mapped. The complete intermediate connection is visible; tributary names are not assigned to the selected mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Sinos entry and terminal delta
correspondence.finding: The Caí approaches from the northwest/west and Sinos from the north along the Canoas–Nova Santa Rita side. Both enter the northern Jacuí delta, which has multiple channels around islands before opening into Guaíba farther south. The selected ending is in the delta, not the distant Atlantic coast. IBGE's original map provides actual channel/island geography; SGB's p.33 single-line drawing independently explains the system relationship, and the annotated Google Earth reproduction on p.50 is only supplementary terminal context.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; individual final delta-channel naming left unassigned

finding: The retained fragment begins with a short westward branch and then turns southeast toward the following boundary-aligned fragment.
The neighboring primary map labels Estero El Empalme and Río Colorado, but those named watercourses lie west of the selected initial setting. No label is transferred to this fragment.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected fragment reviewed against the primary eastern hydrographic view and bounded upper-basin scientific map; exact initial-channel correspondence remains unresolved.

finding: The selected southward boundary-aligned curve is east of the mapped Colorado valley. Its stored border-aligned flag is model metadata rather than primary evidence of a natural watercourse.

The scientific relief figure identifies the high mountain La Laguna catchment, but does not provide enough locatable drainage detail to classify this entire connector as a mapped non-channel crossing.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected extent falls in the inspected eastern hydrographic view; insufficient natural-channel or ridge correspondence.

finding: After the unaccounted eastern approach, the selected route reaches the lower Colorado/La Gloria setting and turns north through La Laguna reservoir. COT shows the elongated reservoir between the mapped inlet and outlet approaches.
La Laguna continues north to Toro; the combined Turbio turns west and then south past the Incaguas, Guanta and Calvario settings. Claro joins near Rivadavia, after which the selected river is Elqui.

The westward Elqui corridor passes the Vicuña reach and Puclaro reservoir, then the Marquesa and Santa Gracia settings toward La Serena. The lower braided/coastal approach and receiving Pacific setting were read at ordinary generalized scale.
COT corroborates the Puclaro waterbody and coastal land margin. It does not itself supply hydronyms, exact estuary channels or present water levels.
correspondence.correspondence: Initial westward connection remains incomplete; the subsequent valley corridor, both reservoir passages, major junctions and actual coast are supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Multiple component names; Elqui is supported only for the downstream receiving river.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: La Laguna–Turbio–Elqui corridor after the unresolved initial connector

correspondence.component_scope: Initial eastward upland feeder and eastern return bend
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the upland stream/pond belt south of the Indian Lake context and northeast of Little Grand Lake. Detailed provincial Map 2009-30 covers its western portions, but the initial eastward bow passes beyond that sheet edge before turning southwest. Organ and Dyke Figure 1 supplies regional terrain/lake context only. The complete out-of-sheet stream connector is not actually read.
correspondence.limits: The gap is a stream/pond connection at ordinary component scale, not a demand for precise bank, vertex or mouth agreement. Unknown opening and small pond names remain null.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward feeder, Little Grand Lake passage and outlet
correspondence.finding: Beyond the unresolved eastern bow, the westward approach to Little Grand Lake, elongated lake passage and northward outlet toward the southwestern Grand Lake basin are readable. Batterson Figure 1 identifies Lewaseechjeech Brook on the eastern approach; Map 2009-30 separately labels Little Grand Lake and Lewaseechjeech Brook in the lake/outlet corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale outside the upstream gap
correspondence.limits: The brook label is retained as a component observation; it does not establish the exact name boundary across all lake passages or the initial branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Grand Lake passage beside Glover Island to northern outlet setting
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor enters the southwestern Grand Lake basin, continues northeast through the lake on the southeastern side of Glover Island, then along the principal Grand Lake body to its northern outlet setting. Glover Island and the western lake arm remain separate geographic context. The selected route does not ascend the separately depicted Hinds Lake, Sandy Lake or Birchy Lake tributary systems.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Grand Lake is a lake/reservoir passage, not a scalar river name. Dam-related historical enlargement and adjacent lake connections are acknowledged without mapping every lake reach to Humber River.

correspondence.component_scope: Junction Brook, main-dam outlet/spillway and Upper Humber junction
correspondence.finding: The selected northward-then-westward corridor corresponds to the Junction Brook route toward the Upper Humber upstream of Deer Lake. This differs geographically from the separate Humber Canal route to Deer Lake. The 1987 primary hydrotechnical account describes the 1925 Junction Brook dam/diversion and identifies the main-dam spillway among Grand Lake outlet modes.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The modeled route through the dam/spillway corridor is not asserted to carry the entire present Grand Lake discharge or to be continuously free-flowing. No present gate or flow condition is established. The Upper Humber approach from the north is not the selected headwater.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Humber below Junction Brook and Deer Lake passage
correspondence.finding: From the Junction Brook/Upper Humber junction, the selected route follows the downstream Upper Humber approach into northeastern Deer Lake, traverses Deer Lake southwestward and reaches its southwestern outlet. The original provincial map distinguishes the river approach, lake body, and downstream river.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Deer Lake is a distinct lake passage. The Upper Humber name is not applied to Grand Lake, the southern feeder or the complete modeled selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Humber to actual Humber Arm ending
correspondence.finding: After leaving southwestern Deer Lake, the selected route follows the lower Humber corridor past Little Rapids and Steady Brook through the Corner Brook/Humber gorge setting and ends at the inner Humber Arm of Bay of Islands. This actual terminal differs from the inland lakes and from adjoining Goose Arm or Middle Arm.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Generalized terminal-setting correspondence only; no exact surveyed mouth, tidal boundary or bank agreement is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward minor drainage south of Cícero Dantas and west/northwest of Heliópolis
correspondence.finding: The first selected section lies in the rural headward drainage around the Serra dos Correia/Calombi–Farmácia setting, continuing south and then east into the Heliópolis tributary corridor. The 2010 IBGE sheet supplies the minor intermittent drainage omitted from the coarser regional map; the 2020 municipal map is substantially more selective and is not used to infer absent minor channels.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized headward-component scale
correspondence.name_scope: Unlabeled initial feeder; geographical identification without a hydronym assertion.

correspondence.component_scope: Heliópolis tributary connection into the Real border river
correspondence.finding: The selected route takes the Jibóia-side drainage south of Heliópolis, crosses the Tamarindo/Jibóia rural setting and joins the receiving Cumbanzê corridor, which reaches the Rio Real near the Rio Real locality/Encontro das Águas sector. It does not take the more northeasterly Rio do Saco/Poço Verde head branch. INEMA shows the Jibóia tributary joining the north–south trunk and distinguishes the Baixa do Tubarão branch farther southwest. The original IBGE 2010 sheet shows Pindorama on the different branch near Heliópolis, outside this selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized corridor and junction scale
correspondence.name_scope: Source labels are component-specific; no exact name-transition position is asserted.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Pindorama is an adjacent branch impoundment, not a selected lake passage. No major reservoir/lake traverse interrupts the selected upper connection at the inspected scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Rio Real border corridor to Tobias Barreto/Itapicuru
correspondence.finding: The selected line turns into the south/southeast-running border river. INEMA repeatedly prints Rio Real and maps its Baixa do Cabo Verde, Muniz/Roncador and Estiva/Negro-side connections. CPRM independently depicts the same corridor, the Mocambo and Jabiberi tributary junction settings on the Sergipe side, and the passage through Tobias Barreto/Fazenda Tourão. The INEMA 2012 field-monitoring table places its Real sampling station on the Bahia–Sergipe divide between Itapicuru and Tobias Barreto.
correspondence.name_scope: Main middle border-river reach, not its side tributaries.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Jabiberi is a separately mapped tributary. The Sergipe 2021 plan lists the Jabiberi reservoir at Tobias Barreto; this is contextual branch infrastructure, not a lake connector followed by the selected mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Real past Rio Real and Jandaíra municipalities
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues southeast past the Rio Real municipality setting and then bends east along northern Jandaíra. INEMA depicts the meandering border river and the Raposo junction; CPRM supplies the Itamirim-side tributary setting and keeps the lower Tabatinga/Macanaír drainage distinct. IBGE Jandaíra shows the lower meanders and continuation through the Cachoeira/Abadia–Indiaroba setting. The Monitora table separately identifies a Rio Real station under the BA-099 bridge at Jandaíra and the off-mainstem Fonte Branca/Rio Real-city reservoir station.
correspondence.name_scope: Lower main river; Fonte Branca reservoir, Raposo, Itamirim and Tabatinga/Macanaír are not uniformly relabeled.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: No mainstem lake-chain passage is required. The separately sampled Fonte Branca impoundment near Rio Real town is off the selected line.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal within the Rio Real estuary
correspondence.finding: The selected endpoint falls in the lower river's broad estuarine widening east of Indiaroba, before the northeastward continuation toward Pontal and Mangue Seco. INEMA and IBGE Jandaíra map this widening as Rio Real and show islands/side channels, the coastal sand barrier and the remaining estuarine continuation to the Atlantic entrance. IBGE labels the northern Piauí-side channels as well. The Sergipe plan explicitly describes the shared Mangue Seco estuary of Real and Piauí; CEMAVE additionally identifies the Piauí–Fundo–Real estuarine complex. These are receiving-setting observations, not a claim that the selected line extends to all of those waters.
correspondence.terminal_setting: Broad tidal estuarine reach connected to the Mangue Seco/Piauí–Fundo–Real complex and Atlantic; selected model endpoint is upstream of the open-sea entrance.
